project.title: Smart Farm Space Diagnosis and Cultivation Environment Monitoring Service
project.summary: A web-based integrated solution that diagnoses whether unused urban spaces are suitable for smart farm conversion and monitors cultivation environments after installation. A single hardware kit collects environmental and soil data, while software calculates suitability scores, recommends improvements, estimates setup costs, visualizes data, and sends alerts.

marketAndPolicyContext.marketTrend: Smart farms are positioned as a key technology for sustainable agriculture under climate crisis and food security concerns.
marketAndPolicyContext.technologyTrend: IoT, big data, and AI are used to precisely measure crop growth environments and optimize resource input.
marketAndPolicyContext.spaceOpportunity: Vertical farming and controlled-environment agriculture can convert rooftops, basements, vacant rooms, and other unused urban spaces into agricultural production spaces.
marketAndPolicyContext.policyContext: The source document references Korea's First Smart Agriculture Promotion Basic Plan for 2025 to 2029 as a national smart agriculture transition strategy.

problemStatement.context: Smart farms are becoming important for sustainable agriculture, but existing solutions mainly focus on post-installation automation and monitoring.
painPoints: Users cannot objectively determine whether an unused urban space is suitable for crop cultivation before investing in smart farm equipment.
Urban spaces such as rooftops, basements, and vacant rooms differ greatly in light, ventilation, temperature, humidity, air quality, and soil conditions.
Uniform equipment installation can cause excessive lighting, heating, cooling, or ventilation costs.
Raw sensor values are difficult for non-experts to interpret.
There is a need to connect pre-installation diagnosis with post-installation monitoring in one lifecycle platform.

targetUsers: Individuals or small businesses considering urban farming
Local institutions interested in urban regeneration or local food production
Non-expert users who need intuitive diagnosis and monitoring

userRequirements.name: Space suitability diagnosis
userRequirements.description: Users need an objective diagnosis of whether candidate spaces such as rooftops, basements, or vacant rooms are suitable for crop cultivation based on combined environmental factors.

userRequirements.name: Improvement and setup cost prediction
userRequirements.description: Users need to know which environmental factors must be improved and how much the required equipment or construction may cost before installation.

userRequirements.name: Optimized setup planning
userRequirements.description: Users need equipment recommendations that match the weaknesses of each space, reducing unnecessary investment.

userRequirements.name: Intuitive decision support
userRequirements.description: Users need score, graph, and color-based reports instead of raw sensor values.

userRequirements.name: Real-time cultivation monitoring
userRequirements.description: Users need continuous monitoring after cultivation begins and alerts for risks such as rapid soil moisture decrease or abnormal temperature.

functionalRequirements.name: Environmental data collection
functionalRequirements.description: Measure air temperature, humidity, CO2 or air quality, fine dust or pollution level, light intensity, noise, soil moisture, and soil temperature.

functionalRequirements.name: Data transmission
functionalRequirements.description: Periodically transmit collected sensor data to the server over Wi-Fi, using MQTT as the lightweight IoT messaging protocol.

functionalRequirements.name: Space suitability diagnosis
functionalRequirements.description: Compare collected sensor data with crop-specific optimal cultivation environment data and calculate a suitability score.

functionalRequirements.name: Improvement analysis
functionalRequirements.description: Analyze insufficient environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, light, ventilation, and air quality, then provide improvement directions.

functionalRequirements.name: Expected setup cost calculation
functionalRequirements.description: Estimate equipment and action costs based on the required improvements.

functionalRequirements.name: Dashboard
functionalRequirements.description: Visualize real-time environmental data, suitability results, environmental deviations, historical trends, and improvement recommendations.

functionalRequirements.name: Notification service
functionalRequirements.description: Send push notifications when thresholds are exceeded or abnormal states are detected.

functionalRequirements.name: History management
functionalRequirements.description: Store space diagnosis history and cultivation-period environmental logs.

functionalRequirements.name: Crop recommendation
functionalRequirements.description: Recommend crops that match the diagnosed space conditions and help users select crops with lower improvement cost and higher expected feasibility.

dataFlow.name: Sensor measurement

inputVariables: Light intensity or daily light integral

partialScoreMethod.transitionMethod: Linear interpolation between optimal and unsuitable ranges

suitabilityScoring.formula: suitabilityScore = (wTemperature * temperatureScore + wHumidity * humidityScore + wLight * lightScore + wCO2 * co2Score) * pollutionCorrectionFactor
constraints: Each partial score must be between 0.0 and 1.0.
The sum of all weights must be 1.0.
The pollution correction factor must be between 0.0 and 1.0.
Better air quality should produce a pollution correction factor closer to 1.0.
validation: Compare public crop-growth reference data with actual sensor readings.
Verify that spaces close to the optimal crop environment produce high scores.
Verify that spaces with clear constraints such as insufficient light or poor ventilation produce low scores.

costPrediction.basis: Use suitability scoring results to identify deficient environmental factors, then map each deficiency to physical improvement equipment or actions.

deficiencyMapping.quantityBasis: Space conditions and required air circulation improvement
Space scale and target humidity range

priceDataProcessing: Detect and adjust abnormally low or high prices.

validation: Compare predicted equipment costs with actual market price ranges.

competitiveDifferentiators.name: Pre-installation diagnosis focus
competitiveDifferentiators.description: Unlike existing smart farm solutions that mainly optimize operation after installation, this service diagnoses whether a candidate urban space is suitable before equipment investment.

competitiveDifferentiators.name: Quantitative suitability and deviation reporting
competitiveDifferentiators.description: The service combines multi-dimensional environmental data such as temperature, humidity, light, CO2, fine dust, and noise with crop-specific cultivation criteria to provide suitability scores and factor-level deviations.

competitiveDifferentiators.name: Non-expert decision reports
competitiveDifferentiators.description: Instead of listing raw sensor values, the dashboard presents score, graph, and color-based reports with improvement priorities.

competitiveDifferentiators.name: Crop-growth domain logic plus AI-assisted analysis
competitiveDifferentiators.description: The diagnosis engine is intended to go beyond simple threshold comparison by structuring crop-growth conditions, sensor data, and space environment information.

competitiveDifferentiators.name: One integrated kit for diagnosis and monitoring
competitiveDifferentiators.description: The same hardware concept connects pre-installation space analysis with post-installation soil and cultivation environment monitoring.

competitiveDifferentiators.name: Expanded target market
competitiveDifferentiators.description: The service targets urban space owners, individuals, small businesses, and local institutions, not only large professional farms.

openIssues.description: The source document mentions both Arduino UNO R4 WiFi and ESP32-based sensor kits. The final implementation should choose one board or explicitly define both variants.
The requirements include CO2 measurement, while the explicit sensor table lists MQ135 for air quality. A dedicated CO2 sensor model should be finalized if accurate CO2 concentration is required.
The document mentions PostgreSQL in one section and PostgreSQL/MySQL in another. The final backend specification should choose the primary relational database.
InfluxDB is described as a planned or optional expansion. The implementation should decide whether it is required for the initial prototype.

openIssues.topic: Sensor count and missing explicit sensor models
openIssues.description: The source describes an ESP32-based seven-sensor kit including CO2 and fine dust, but the detailed sensor table lists six explicit sensor models. Dedicated CO2 and fine-dust sensor models should be finalized if those values are required as direct measurements.
The text table lists EF04027 for soil moisture, while the embedded circuit diagram visually shows a SparkFun Soil Moisture Sensor. The final bill of materials should choose the exact model.

The embedded hardware diagram was reviewed and its components were recorded, but exact pin-to-sensor mapping should be confirmed manually from the original diagram or hardware design file because the image has overlapping wires.
The source includes a month/week schedule table, but extracted text did not preserve the marked week ranges. Exact scheduling should be confirmed from the original HWP if needed.
